title: Linezolid
dek: Oxazolidinone, 50S PTC, Group A. WHO BPaLM dose 600 mg daily. Myelosuppression and neuropathy limit duration. rplC/rrl resistance is still uncommon — toxicity is not.
story: Linezolid is a protein-synthesis inhibitor that became Group A because it is bactericidal against Mtb and because Nix/ZeNix/PRACTECAL needed a third (or fourth) solid drug. WHO dose inside BPaLM/BPaL is 600 mg once daily, not the 1200 mg Nix-TB start as routine. Some 9-month recipes use 600 mg then step down.

Mitochondrial toxicity in the host looks like the bacterial mechanism: marrow suppression (watch FBC), peripheral and optic neuropathy, lactic acidosis rarely. TDM (trough <2 µg/mL in some US expert practice) is how you keep the drug for 26 weeks.
Resistance genes rplC/rrl are sparse in surveys — for now. A WT ribosome does not mean you get to ignore the platelet count. SSRIs and LZD risk serotonin syndrome — a med-rec issue, not a BAM issue.
deep: Dropping LZD at week 8 because of anaemia without a replacement is how BPaL becomes BDQ+Pa. Plan the off-ramp before the haemoglobin does.
Tedizolid is not a WHO substitute by default.
Pregnancy: used in Pa-sparing constructs; PK may shift by trimester.

visual.caption: Schematic tension between antimycobacterial dose and host mitochondrial toxicity. 600 mg is the WHO compromise; 1200 mg cured in Nix and injured more hosts.

steps.body: A planned interruption with close cultures ≠ silently remaining on two drugs for a month.

steps.title: Neuropathy may not reverse as fast as platelets

example.takeaway: LZD’s limiting reagent is often the host mitochondrion, not rplC.

choices: 1200 mg daily as the default for 6 months
